comparisons.evidence: Q covers additional causal mechanisms such as reducing procedural uncertainty through an “appointment rehearsal,” explaining clinical purpose, creating a “same-day recovery queue,” and addressing fear with a nurse or peer navigator. P is broad but consolidates more heavily around scheduling, routing, and capacity recovery.

P moves beyond ordinary attendance tactics by treating missed attendance as a fault-tolerance problem: “completing the next clinically useful step,” making “the household” the scheduling unit, and targeting the hospital’s own unreliability. Q has strong ideas, but more of them resemble advanced versions of familiar flexible booking and patient-support practices.

P explicitly extracts rules from “Fault-tolerant computing” and “Theme parks,” including “Graceful degradation,” “Redundancy,” and “Virtual queues,” then maps them into concrete mechanisms. Q’s industry analogy—“Airlines, restaurants, and ticketing systems”—supports the exchange idea but remains a loose comparison rather than a worked structural transfer.

Both select early uncertainty capture, but P pairs it tightly with recoverable capacity: “an ‘unsure’ patient is not yet a no-show” and the slot can be reclaimed immediately. It also recommends measuring “completed care episodes within 7 and 30 days,” avoiding the narrower optimization of Q’s primary metric, “unused clinician capacity.”

P states testable assumptions and concrete failure modes for every survivor, such as “arrival bunching,” “gaming,” “privacy concerns,” “low route density,” and digital exclusion. Q mainly assigns difficulty labels and gives benefits; it does not comparably interrogate how its finalists could fail.

P states precise mechanism-level insights: uncertainty is “a recoverable state,” “Attendance is not binary,” and hospital delays can train patients to treat times as approximate. Q articulates useful reframings such as a “transferable reservation,” but its practical rationale is less sharply separated from the feature description.

note: P is stronger at disciplined cross-domain derivation, explicit falsifiability, and metric reframing; Q has slightly wider human and behavioural coverage.
